test_title: PYST 4: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A person drives to his office at 40 km/h and reaches 15 minutes late. If he drives at 60 km/h, he reaches 10 minutes early. What is the distance to his office?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Distance = [Product of Speeds ÷ Difference of Speeds] × Time Difference

Time Difference = 15 min (late) + 10 min (early) = 25 min = 25/60 hours

Distance = [40 × 60 ÷ (60 − 40)] × 25/60

Distance = [2400 ÷ 20] × 25/60 = 120 × 25/60 = 50 km

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed 1 (S₁) = 40 km/h, Time 1 = Actual Time + 15 min

Speed 2 (S₂) = 60 km/h, Time 2 = Actual Time − 10 min

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5f4d50a7072e460683eaa258cf16d83fa41027fd5aa0b48bbd299eb315b9ee0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance to the office be D km.

⇒ Time taken at 40 km/h = D/40 hours.

⇒ Time taken at 60 km/h = D/60 hours.

⇒ Total difference in time = 15 minutes (late) + 10 minutes (early) = 25 minutes.

⇒ Converting time difference to hours: 25/60 = 5/12 hours.

⇒ D/40 − D/60 = 5/12

⇒ (3D − 2D) / 120 = 5/12

⇒ D / 120 = 5/12

⇒ D = (5 × 120) / 12

⇒ D = 5 × 10 = 50 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

When a journey is divided into two equal distances traveled at speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Speed-Time Proportionality

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time. If the ratio of speeds is a:b, the ratio of time taken is b:a.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (S₁ − S₂). In opposite directions, it is the sum (S₁ + S₂).</p
